input.headline: California law takes effect requiring real estate agents to disclose digitally or AI-altered listing images and link to the original unaltered photos, enforced via licensing discipline.

input_full.excerpt: An act to require disclosure of digitally altered real-estate images. It requires real estate brokers, salespersons, and persons acting on their behalf who include a digitally altered image (including AI-altered images) in advertising or promotional material for the sale of real property to disclose that the image has been altered and to provide a link, URL, or QR code to a publicly accessible copy of the original, unaltered image. It is enforced through disciplinary action under the California Real Estate Regulations, including potential license suspension or revocation.
input_full.headline: Real Estate Digitally Altered Images Disclosures (AB 723)
